title: Handling User Input
description: Learn how to collect and process form submissions in ASP.NET Core MVC using model binding, validation, and the POST-RedIRECT-GET pattern. Includes practical form examples with validation feedback.

blocks.text: Most web applications need to **collect information from users** — a contact form, a product search, a registration page, or a checkout process. ASP.NET Core handles user input through **model binding** (converting request data into C# objects) and **validation** (ensuring the data meets your business rules).
In this lesson, you will learn how to build HTML forms, receive form data in controller actions, validate the input, and give users clear feedback when something goes wrong.

Before diving into code, it is important to understand the standard pattern for handling form submissions: **POST-Redirect-GET (PRG)**. When a user submits a form (POST), your action processes the data. If successful, it redirects to a GET action (showing a confirmation page or the updated list). If validation fails, it re-renders the form with error messages.

blocks.title: Why POST-Redirect-GET matters
items: Prevents duplicate submissions when the user refreshes the page
Provides a clean URL after form submission
Separates the form display (GET) from form processing (POST)
Keeps the browser history clean and predictable

blocks.text: ASP.NET Core provides **Tag Helpers** that make building forms easy. The `<form>` Tag Helper generates the correct `action` and `method` attributes, while `<input asp-for>` and `<span asp-validation-for>` automatically bind to your model and display validation messages.

blocks.text: Receiving Form Data in a Controller
When the form is submitted, ASP.NET Core's model binding automatically maps the form fields to a C# object. You simply declare the model type as a parameter in your POST action.

blocks.title: The ContactForm model and POST action
blocks.content: Define a model with validation attributes, then receive and validate it in a POST action.

blocks.title: Always validate with ModelState.IsValid
blocks.text: Never process form data without first checking `ModelState.IsValid`. Data annotation attributes like `[Required]` and `[EmailAddress]` run automatically during model binding. If any validation rule fails, `ModelState.IsValid` returns false and the error messages are available in the view.

ASP.NET Core includes built-in validation attributes that you can apply directly to model properties. These attributes enforce rules declaratively, so you do not need to write manual validation logic in every action.

blocks.title: Common validation attributes
items: **[Required]** — The field must have a value
**[StringLength(max)]** — Limits the character count of a string
**[Range(min, max)]** — Requires a numeric or date value within a range
**[EmailAddress]** — Validates that the value is a properly formatted email address
**[Compare("OtherProperty")]** — Ensures two fields match (e.g., password confirmation)
**[RegularExpression(pattern)]** — Validates the value against a regex pattern

blocks.text: When `ModelState.IsValid` is false, the error messages from validation attributes are automatically displayed in the view where you placed `<span asp-validation-for>` elements. The validation scripts partial (`_ValidationScriptsPartial.cshtml`) enables client-side validation so errors appear immediately without a page reload.

blocks.title: Client-side vs. server-side validation
blocks.text: Client-side validation provides instant feedback and reduces unnecessary server requests. However, it is not a security measure — a user can bypass client-side validation by crafting their own HTTP request. Always validate on the server side as well.

The `[ValidateAntiForgeryToken]` attribute on POST actions and the `@addTagHelper` in forms work together to prevent **Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)** attacks. The form Tag Helper automatically generates a hidden anti-forgery token, and the action attribute validates it. Always include both.

terms.definition: The automatic process of converting HTTP request data (form fields, query strings, route values) into .NET objects that action methods accept as parameters.
A dictionary that tracks validation state. ModelState.IsValid is true when all validation rules pass; false when any rule fails.
Attributes applied to model properties (e.g., [Required], [EmailAddress]) that declare validation rules declaratively.
A pattern where a POST action processes data and redirects to a GET action, preventing duplicate submissions and keeping URLs clean.
A hidden form field that prevents Cross-Site Request Forgery attacks. Generated automatically by the form Tag Helper and validated by [ValidateAntiForgeryToken].

blocks.title: Build a Contact Form with Validation
blocks.description: Create a contact form that collects a name, email, and message, with full validation and success feedback.
steps: Create a ContactForm model in the Models folder with Name, Email, and Message properties
Add [Required] and [EmailAddress] validation attributes to the appropriate properties
Create a Contact action in HomeController with both GET and POST versions
In the GET action, return the empty contact form view
In the POST action, accept ContactForm as a parameter, check ModelState.IsValid, and redirect on success
Create Views/Home/Contact.cshtml with a form using Tag Helpers (asp-for, asp-validation-for)
Add _ValidationScriptsPartial at the bottom of the view for client-side validation
Run the app, submit an empty form, and confirm validation error messages appear
blocks.expectedOutcome: Submitting an empty form displays client-side validation errors. Submitting valid data redirects to the Contact page with a success message. The form uses Tag Helpers and validation attributes throughout.

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: The POST-Redirect-GET pattern separates form display (GET) from form processing (POST)
Model binding automatically converts form data into C# objects passed to action parameters
Data annotation attributes like [Required] and [EmailAddress] declare validation rules on model properties
ModelState.IsValid checks whether all validation rules passed before processing data
Tag Helpers (asp-for, asp-validation-for) generate correct HTML and wire up validation automatically
Always use [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] on POST actions to prevent CSRF attacks
blocks.takeaway: Handling user input safely is one of the most critical skills in web development. ASP.NET Core's model binding and validation system provides a robust, declarative approach that protects both your application and your users.
